title: Giving up music and the Rhapsodians
summary: On arriving he had left his violin behind and meant to quit, but the 12-piece Rhapsodians pressed him to join, and Beansie offered to buy a violin.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So when did you finally get your bass? Did you have a bass over in Pasch-Christian or wait until you got over here? Yeah, I know I had bass in Pasch-Christian. Man.

I had, I had several basses in Pasch-Christian. I had basses that they, they broke up for me and then I, I, I left a piece of bass in Pasch-Christian when I came here. Well, when I came here, I gave up music. I didn't intend to play anymore. Oh really? No, I didn't intend to play anymore. Well, after I got here and I began to go around and mix with different people, then they, we could, they got up a band by the name of the Rapsodians.
No, I imagine you didn't. I don't think you were here.
No, I know I wasn't ever around in those days.

No. Well, we had, we have a 12 piece band and their name was the Rapsodians and they kept on after me, kept on after me to, they heard about me and kept on after me to, to play with them. I said, well, I don't have any violin while I left my violin in Pasch-Christian.

And I, I didn't care about playing anymore. Well, after I didn't care about playing anymore, they say, well, beans is there, I'll buy your violin. Well, I say, I don't have any money, which I didn't have. Then I was so independent then, I didn't think credit count was any way. And I was sticking on my chest. Who me? No, indeed. I don't want you to buy me no violin. I, what I get, I'll pay cash for it. Well, I was thinking that if you was a big shot, you pay for what you're getting. That was over with, but that wasn't anything. And I went to a wire line and they asked me about my credit card. I said, I don't have any. I thought I was smart. You understand? I said, what I get, I'll pay for it. I was sticking out my chest. I pay for what I get and I don't, I don't get nothing on credit. Smart, you understand? I thought I was smart, but I was dumb. And they told me, he said, now, Handy, I'm going to tell you, see, if you don't have a credit card you're not recognized. See, they have people really have nothing but some money and they have a credit account because they wanted their name to be enlisted in the book to be recognized as someone. Well, I still couldn't see it. You understand? Well, I still take me that, that granted that I had, I was something that could stick out my chest pocket here for everything I'll get.
